title: dedicated-fleet-autoscaler: add burst controls, throughput guarantees, and utilization reporting
author: Riley Chen
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets need predictable per-customer throughput guarantees while allowing short-term bursts to absorb spikes. This PR implements burst controls and explicit throughput guarantees in the dedicated fleet autoscaler, and augments utilization reporting so SRE and console users can reason about burst consumption, guaranteed vs. best-effort capacity, and throttling events.

What changed:
- Autoscaler: introduce new policy knobs: `min_guaranteed_tps`, `burst_capacity`, `burst_window_seconds`, and `burst_recovery_rate`. The autoscaler will ensure guaranteed capacity is preserved while permitting short bursts using a token-bucket accounting model.
- Routing/fallback: when guaranteed capacity is saturated, requests can be routed to best-effort pools or fall back to compatible model variants per policy.
- Telemetry: emit new metrics `dedicated.autoscaler.guaranteed_tps`, `dedicated.autoscaler.burst_tokens`, `dedicated.autoscaler.burst_used`, `dedicated.autoscaler.throttle_events` and expose them to the Console and metrics backend (Prometheus + internal ingestion).
- Console: add a new dashboard and per-fleet panels for burst utilization and guaranteed capacity headroom.
- Reporting: update fleet utilization report generation to include burst accounting and actionable recommendations for resizing or purchasing burst add-ons.
- Tests: integration tests for token-bucket behavior and e2e scenario tests for routing when guarantees are hit.

Notes:
- The description contains high-level rationale and configuration examples. See docs/dedicated/autoscaling.md for operator-facing details.
- Backwards compatibility: existing autoscaler configs continue to work; new fields are optional.

Files changed (high-level): services/dedicated-autoscaler/autoscaler.go, services/dedicated-autoscaler/policy.go, services/dedicated-autoscaler/token_bucket.go, infra/telemetry/metrics_exporter.go, console/dashboards/dedicated_autoscaler.json, docs/dedicated/autoscaling.md, tests/integration/test_autoscaler_token_bucket.py, tests/e2e/test_guarantee_routing.py, config/examples/dedicated_policy.yaml, CHANGELOG.md
commits: Initialize burst control primitives and policy parsing - add policy struct fields - basic token-bucket implementation
Add metrics and Console dashboard integration - export new metrics to Prometheus - wire to console data source - add dashboard JSON
Tests, docs, and config examples - add integration + e2e tests - update dedicated autoscaling docs and changelog - small refactors from review feedback
review_comments: Marta Lopez: Can we make burst_window_seconds bounded (max 3600s) to avoid very long borrow periods? Also please add unit tests for edge cases where burst_capacity >> fleet size.

Riley Chen (author): Added validation to policy.go to cap burst_window_seconds at 3600s and extended token-bucket tests to include large burst_capacity scenarios (tests/integration/test_autoscaler_token_bucket.py).
Owen Park: Metrics look good; request that `burst_tokens` be a gauge and `burst_used` be a counter. Also call out cardinality in the telemetry comment so we don't tag by request id.

Riley Chen (author): Switched `burst_tokens` -> gauge and `burst_used` -> counter. Added comment in metrics_exporter.go to discourage high-cardinality labels. CI initially failed lint for dashboard JSON formatting, then pass after fix.

Samira Khan: Suggest adding a small safety: when min_guaranteed_tps is increased, we wait a grace period before shrinking best-effort capacity to avoid immediate throttling during transient config changes.
Riley Chen (author): Implemented a 30s grace window when decreasing best-effort allocation; documented in autoscaling.md.
ci_log_summary: CI pipeline: lint -> unit -> integration -> e2e. Initial run: lint failed on console dashboard JSON; subsequent commit fixed formatting and all pipelines passed. Prometheus integration tests passed in CI staging.
